findings.message: The received file has the required 1536x1024 landscape canvas, no alpha channel, exactly three separated studies, no characters, and no story action.
The repeated arched windows, tiled wall band, iron-column rhythm, roof structure, clocks, and Cafe Siete grille make the three studies read more consistently as one station than the v002 return.

The finish remains a blocking mismatch. Dense all-over architectural detail, continuous modeled gray, realistic material texture, and deep perspective make the sheet read as a monochrome architectural visualization or engraving rather than clean flat printed-manga line art.

The ticket-hall, cafe, and platform floors still contain mirror-like dark puddles, long white highlight streaks, reflected structural shapes, and wet-tile shine. These directly violate the required matte contour puddles and prohibitions on reflected scenery, gloss, and specular lighting.

Compared with the two approved finish examples, the candidate still lacks sufficiently open white paper, decisive selective black shapes, quiet secondary surfaces, and clearly bounded screentone regions. Texture and line density remain evenly distributed, weakening manga-style focal hierarchy.

The result remains extremely close to the rejected v002 architecture, camera placement, surface modeling, and reflective-floor treatment. Although the pixels differ and some areas are lighter, the visual result does not demonstrate the required full redraw away from the rejected cinematic finish.

The large ticket-hall clock still does not read unmistakably as 12:07. Its long hand remains near the five-minute position at numeral I instead of visibly between I and II at the seven-minute position.

The PNG is encoded as RGB and its channels are not identical. Mean RGB values are approximately 134.78, 133.49, and 131.67, with a maximum red-blue difference of 20, so the image retains a subtle warm tint and does not satisfy the true grayscale/no-tint output contract.
No image was edited, filtered, regenerated, converted, renamed, or promoted during review. Byte-identical copies are retained only for review evidence and possible correction input.
